sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的临时博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the Trump administration rolls back two more of President Obama's signature achievements.
sentences.zh: 今天，特朗普政府撤销了奥巴马总统的两项标志性成就。

sentences.en: Repealing the Clean Power Plan, calling it a war on coal, and ending a federal requirement that employers provide birth control coverage,
sentences.zh: 废除《清洁电力计划》，称其为对煤炭的战争，并结束了联邦政府要求雇主提供避孕保险的规定，

sentences.en: saying we will not allow people of faith to be targeted, bullied, or silenced anymore.
sentences.zh: 声称我们绝不再允许有信仰的人受到针对、欺凌或噤声。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, October 10th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月10日，星期二。

sentences.en: I'm from this wonderful Commonwealth.
sentences.zh: 我来自这个美好的联邦州。

sentences.en: It is good to be back home.
sentences.zh: 回到家乡的感觉真好。

sentences.en: Lisa Friedman, what is the head of the EPA, Scott Pruitt, doing in Hazard, Kentucky on Monday?
sentences.zh: 丽莎·弗里德曼，美国环保署署长斯科特·普鲁特周一在肯塔基州的哈泽德做什么？

sentences.en: Scott Pruitt went to the heart of coal country for one big reason, to tell them...
sentences.zh: 斯科特·普鲁特深入煤炭之乡只有一个主要原因，那就是告诉他们……

sentences.en: Here's the president's message.
sentences.zh: 这是总统的信息。

sentences.en: The war on coal is over.
sentences.zh: 煤炭战争结束了。

sentences.en: You know, in regulatory terms, what he means by that is that the administration is taking the first real steps
sentences.zh: 你知道，从监管角度来看，他的意思是政府正在采取真正的第一步，

sentences.en: in repealing former President Obama's signature climate change regulation, a sweeping regulation that would have reined in carbon emissions from coal-fired power plants.
sentences.zh: 以废除前总统奥巴马标志性的气候变化法规，这是一项旨在遏制燃煤电厂碳排放的全面法规。

sentences.en: And he wanted coal miners in Kentucky to be the first to know.
sentences.zh: 他希望肯塔基州的煤矿工人成为第一批知道这个消息的人。

sentences.en: Tomorrow, in Washington, D.C., I'll be signing a proposed rule to withdraw the so-called Clean Power Plan of the past administration.
sentences.zh: 明天，在华盛顿特区，我将签署一项拟议规则，撤销上届政府所谓的《清洁电力计划》。

sentences.en: What's happening tomorrow and what Scott Pruitt announced today is the beginning of the real work that needs to be done to end that regulation.
sentences.zh: 明天将要发生的事情以及斯科特·普鲁特今天宣布的内容，是结束该法规所需真正工作的开始。

sentences.en: This Clean Power Plan that President Obama put in place, what exactly did it set out to do to the coal industry?
sentences.zh: 奥巴马总统实施的这项《清洁电力计划》，到底打算对煤炭行业做什么？

sentences.en: In technical terms, the Clean Power Plan aimed to cut emissions from the power sector 32% by 2030 from 2005 levels.
sentences.zh: 从技术上讲，《清洁电力计划》旨在到2030年将电力行业的排放量在2005年的基础上削减32%。

sentences.en: So what does that mean in real terms?
sentences.zh: 那么这在实际意义上意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: It meant that every state had to have a plan to shift away from coal to natural gas in some cases, to renewable energy, and the aim was to see a broad transition to cleaner energy.
sentences.zh: 这意味着每个州都必须制定计划，在某些情况下从煤炭转向天然气，转向可再生能源，其目的是实现向更清洁能源的广泛转型。

sentences.en: The past administration was unapologetic.
sentences.zh: 上届政府对此毫不掩饰。

sentences.en: They were using every bit of power, every bit of authority, to use the EPA to pick winners and losers and how we generate electricity in this country.
sentences.zh: 他们动用了所有的权力和权威，利用环保署来挑选赢家和输家，决定我们国家如何发电。

sentences.en: And that's wrong.
sentences.zh: 这是错误的。

sentences.en: In his speech in Kentucky, Scott Pruitt said that the Obama administration was picking and choosing winners in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在肯塔基州的演讲中，斯科特·普鲁特表示，奥巴马政府在《清洁电力计划》中挑选了美国电力行业的赢家和输家。

sentences.en: electricity industry with the Clean Power Plan.
sentences.zh: 这准确吗？

sentences.en: Is that at all accurate?
sentences.zh: 这完全准确吗？

sentences.en: I think it depends.
sentences.zh: 我认为这取决于你怎么看。

sentences.en: You know, there's no question that the Clean Power Plan was aimed at moving the country off coal-fired power plans.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，《清洁电力计划》旨在推动国家摆脱燃煤电厂。

sentences.en: At the same time, we see the administration itself picking winners and losers.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我们看到本届政府自己也在挑选赢家和输家。

sentences.en: As recently as last week, the Department of Energy put forward a proposal to essentially subsidize coal and nuclear energy.
sentences.zh: 就在上周，能源部提出了一项提案，本质上是为了补贴煤炭和核能。

sentences.en: And that has brought about a really odd alliance of renewable energy groups and the oil and gas industry
sentences.zh: 这促成了一个非常奇怪的联盟，由可再生能源团体和石油天然气行业组成，

sentences.en: who are telling the administration, you know, look, you're doing exactly what you accused the Obama administration of doing.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉政府，你看，你们正在做的事情正是你们指责奥巴马政府所做的事情。

sentences.en: So they're just picking different winners.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只是挑选了不同的赢家。

sentences.en: Picking different winners.
sentences.zh: 挑选了不同的赢家。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What we ought to be about as an agency, and this is not the most profound statement you may hear this year, but regulations ought to make things regular.
sentences.zh: 作为政府机构，我们应该做的是——这可能不是你今年听到的最深刻的陈述——但法规应该让事情变得规范。

sentences.en: What does Pruitt mean when he talks about the need to make regulations regular?
sentences.zh: 当普鲁特谈到需要让法规规范化时，他是什么意思？

sentences.en: I mean, the truth is I have no idea what he means.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我不知道他是什么意思。

sentences.en: You know, like every time I've asked for an interview with Scott Pruitt, I'm told some version of, we'll look for some opportunity where the New York Times can be fair to us.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每次我要求采访斯科特·普鲁特时，我得到的答复都是某种版本，比如我们会寻找机会让《纽约时报》对我们公平报道。

sentences.en: But one thing that is clear is that, you know, Scott Pruitt has said from day one that he is taking what he describes as a back-to-basics approach.
sentences.zh: 但有一点很清楚，斯科特·普鲁特从第一天起就说他采取的是他所描述的回归基础的方法。

sentences.en: He sees regulating carbon emissions, he sees dealing with climate change as outside of the bounds of what the EPA is charged with doing.
sentences.zh: 他认为监管碳排放、处理气候变化超出了环保署的职责范围。

sentences.en: He believes the EPA needs to stick to, his words again, making sure there's clean air and clean water.
sentences.zh: 他认为环保署需要坚持——再次引用他的话——确保空气和水是清洁的。

sentences.en: One of the many concerns that raises is that there is a sticky issue that is called the endangerment finding.
sentences.zh: 这引发的众多担忧之一是，有一个被称为“危害认定”的棘手问题。

sentences.en: It's based on a 2009 EPA finding that the EPA does have to regulate carbon emissions.
sentences.zh: 它基于环保署2009年的一项认定，即环保署确实必须监管碳排放。

sentences.en: So the EPA needs a replacement to the clean power plant because under the law, the EPA must regulate carbon emissions.
sentences.zh: 因此，环保署需要一个《清洁电力计划》的替代方案，因为根据法律，环保署必须监管碳排放。

sentences.en: And since coal and coal-fired power plants produce so much carbon emissions, they have to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 由于煤炭和燃煤电厂产生大量的碳排放，他们必须对此采取行动。

sentences.en: That's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 这完全正确。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, what Scott Pruitt is reportedly going to do tomorrow when he formalizes the repeal of the clean power plan
sentences.zh: 现在，据报道，斯科特·普鲁特明天在正式废除《清洁电力计划》时，

sentences.en: is also indicate that the EPA will think about soliciting comments from the public about what could take its place.
sentences.zh: 还将表示环保署将考虑征求公众意见，探讨什么可以取代它。

sentences.en: I think there's a hope within the EPA that that act will satisfy the courts for a while, that they will be able to tell the courts, look, we're looking for a replacement.
sentences.zh: 我认为环保署内部有一种希望，即这一举动能暂时满足法院的要求，他们可以告诉法院，看，我们正在寻找替代方案。

sentences.en: We need to take time and talk to people.
sentences.zh: 我们需要花时间与人们沟通。

sentences.en: Just about everybody I've spoken with, and this is from industry and environmental groups alike, see this as just a clear delaying tactic.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的几乎每个人，无论是行业还是环保团体，都认为这显然是一种拖延战术。

sentences.en: Whether you lament this fact or don't lament this fact, the coal industry in the United States is dying, right?
sentences.zh: 无论你是否为此感到惋惜，美国的煤炭行业正在消亡，对吧？

sentences.en: So what's the significance of replacing the clean power plan?
sentences.zh: 那么，取代《清洁电力计划》的意义何在？

sentences.en: Is it to slow that death, to preserve a few coal-fired power plants, or what exactly?
sentences.zh: 是为了减缓这种消亡，保留几家燃煤电厂，还是其他什么？

sentences.en: So I think the Trump administration would, and they have argued, that they are reviving the coal industry.
sentences.zh: 我认为特朗普政府会辩称，他们正在振兴煤炭行业。

sentences.en: Most energy analysts say that is just not possible.
sentences.zh: 大多数能源分析师认为这根本不可能。

sentences.en: Arrival fossil fuel, natural gas, is somewhat cleaner and dramatically cheaper.
sentences.zh: 另一种化石燃料——天然气，在某种程度上更清洁，而且价格便宜得多。

sentences.en: And in fact, the low price of natural gas is what has been driving most of the shuttering of coal-fired power plants.
sentences.zh: 事实上，天然气的低价正是导致大多数燃煤电厂关闭的主要原因。

sentences.en: I just spoke the other day with DT Energy in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 我前几天刚和密歇根州的DT能源公司谈过。

sentences.en: They are in the process of closing down, I think by 2040, the last few coal-fired power plants they have.
sentences.zh: 他们正在关闭最后几家燃煤电厂，我想是在2040年之前。

sentences.en: And they're kind of agnostic about ending the clean power plan.
sentences.zh: 他们对废除《清洁电力计划》持中立态度。

sentences.en: They say, look, we're moving to cleaner energy because it's better for our business.
sentences.zh: 他们说，看，我们转向清洁能源是因为这对我们的业务更好。

sentences.en: That's a bottom-line decision for them, not a regulatory decision.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说是一个底线决策，而不是监管决策。

sentences.en: And even if it were possible, how can the U.S.
sentences.zh: 即使有可能，美国又怎么能在减少二氧化碳排放的同时振兴煤炭行业呢？

sentences.en: revive the coal industry while also reducing CO2 emissions?
sentences.zh: 这可能吗？

sentences.en: Is that possible?
sentences.zh: 我认为这两者是不可能兼得的。

sentences.en: I think the two things are not possible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，考虑到你所说的撤销这项计划需要多长时间，

sentences.en: I mean, given everything that you've said about how long this will take to rescind,
sentences.zh: 以及煤炭行业暗淡的未来，总统的这一举动，斯科特·普鲁特的这一举动，在很大程度上是象征性的吗？

sentences.en: and about the kind of dim future of coal as an industry, is the president's action here, Scott Pruitt's action, is it largely symbolic?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我和科罗拉多州州长进行过这次谈话，他说他们也在关闭煤电厂。

sentences.en: You know, I had this conversation with the governor of Colorado who was saying that, you know, they too are closing coal plants.
sentences.zh: 他们的风能产业正在起飞。

sentences.en: Their wind industry is taking off.
sentences.zh: 他们正在突飞猛进地增加清洁能源就业岗位。

sentences.en: They are growing clean energy jobs by leaps and bounds.
sentences.zh: 所以，一方面，你是完全正确的。

sentences.en: So, you know, on the one hand, you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 无论有没有《清洁电力计划》，全国几十个州都在发生变化。

sentences.en: Things are happening in dozens of states around the country, whether there's a clean power plan or not.
sentences.zh: 但废除《清洁电力计划》无疑让依赖化石燃料的州更容易暂时不必考虑改变能源结构的负担。

sentences.en: But repealing the clean power plan certainly makes it easier for fossil fuel-reliant states to not have to think about the burden of shifting their energy generation for a while.
sentences.zh: 丽莎，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Lisa, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、扎伊兰·蒙达尼等等。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 我们将直播精选采访，任何人都可以于11月18日在NYTimes.com免费观看。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 你不会想错过的。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 总统认为信仰自由是这个国家的一项基本权利，我想我们所有人也都这么认为。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天所做的一切的意义所在。

sentences.en: The president believes that the freedom to practice one's faith is a fundamental right in this country, and I think all of us do.
sentences.zh: 我们的联邦政府应该始终保护这项权利，只要唐纳德·特朗普担任总统，他就会这样做。

sentences.en: And that's all that today was about.
sentences.zh: 盖尔，特朗普政府周五在避孕问题上做了什么？

sentences.en: Our federal government should always protect that right, and as long as Donald Trump is president, he will.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们基本上通知雇主，如果他们对在医疗计划中涵盖避孕措施有任何宗教异议，

sentences.en: Gail, what did the Trump administration do Friday with respect to birth control?
sentences.zh: 他们就不必再这样做了。

sentences.en: Well, they basically advised employers that if they had any religious objections to covering birth control contraceptives in their health care plans,
sentences.zh: 真的就是这么简单。

sentences.en: that they didn't have to do it anymore.
sentences.zh: 盖尔·柯林斯是《时报》的专栏作家，撰写关于美国政治和文化的文章。

sentences.en: It's as easy as that, really.
sentences.zh: 这是《平价医疗法案》的一部分。

sentences.en: Gail Collins is a columnist for The Times, who writes about American politics and culture.
sentences.zh: 这是奥巴马医改的一部分。

sentences.en: It was part of the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府撤销了奥巴马医改的避孕覆盖强制令，兑现了总统对保守派选民的承诺。

sentences.en: It was a part of Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 宗教团体已经获准拒绝为员工提供他们基于宗教或道德理由反对的服务保险。

sentences.en: The Trump administration has rolled back Obamacare's birth control coverage mandate, fulfilling a vow the president had made to his conservative base.
sentences.zh: 但现在，根据卫生与公众服务部今天发布的一项规则，

sentences.en: Religious groups are already allowed to deny their employees insurance coverage for services they oppose on religious or moral grounds.
sentences.zh: 这些豁免范围已扩大到包括任何有道德异议的公司或非营利组织。

sentences.en: But now, according to a rule released today by the Department of Health and Human Services,
sentences.zh: 所以我对政府最初是如何介入避孕问题的很感兴趣。

sentences.en: those exemptions have been expanded to include any company or nonprofit with moral objections as well.
sentences.zh: 这是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: So I'm interested in how the government came to be involved in birth control in the first place.
sentences.zh: 这要追溯到19世纪70年代初政府取缔避孕措施的时候。

sentences.en: Where does that start?
sentences.zh: 当时兴起了一场社会纯洁运动，他们反对任何避孕方法。

sentences.en: It starts way back with the government outlawing birth control in the early 1870s.
sentences.zh: 他们让政府通过了禁止邮寄的法律，利用邮件，这在当时是分发避孕套或任何其他避孕方法所必需的。

sentences.en: A social purity movement arose, and they disapproved of any methods of birth control.
sentences.zh: 这是一场由一个叫安东尼·康斯托克的人领导的运动。

sentences.en: And they got the government to pass laws against mailing, using the mail, which was what you needed back then in order to distribute condoms or any other method of birth control.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的一句关于安东尼·康斯托克的引语是，当有人问他关于已婚夫妇，以及已婚夫妇是否应该能够获得避孕措施时，

sentences.en: This was a movement run by a guy named Anthony Comstock.
sentences.zh: 如果他们想限制家庭规模，他说，他们难道不能使用自制力吗？还是说他们必须堕落到野兽的水平？

sentences.en: And my favorite quote from Anthony Comstock is when he was asked about married couples and whether married couples shouldn't be able to have some access to birth control
sentences.zh: 这就是社会纯洁运动的基本思维模式。

sentences.en: if they wanted to limit the size of their families, he said, can they not use self-control or must they sink to the level of beasts?
sentences.zh: 我猜野兽就是那些使用避孕措施的人。

sentences.en: And that was the basic kind of thought pattern of the social purity movement.
sentences.zh: 不，野兽基本上是指那些不节制的人。

sentences.en: I guess beasts are those who use birth control.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢的是禁欲。

sentences.en: No, beasts are what people who don't abstain, basically.
sentences.zh: 晚上好。

sentences.en: What they like is abstinence.
sentences.zh: 你即将看到的是一场关于避孕问题的未经排练、未经审查的采访。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 这将是一场关于成人话题的自由讨论，我们认为这个话题值得公众审视。

sentences.en: What you're about to witness is an unrehearsed, uncensored interview on the issue of birth control.
sentences.zh: 当我们进入20世纪20年代时，人们对性的态度要放松得多。

sentences.en: It will be a free discussion of an adult topic, a topic that we feel merits public examination.
sentences.zh: 那时，玛格丽特·桑格在纽约开设了她的第一批诊所。

sentences.en: When we got into the 1920s, people had a much more relaxed attitude towards sex.
sentences.zh: 当玛格丽特·桑格夫人在1916年在美国开设第一家避孕诊所时，“避孕”是一个禁忌词。

sentences.en: And at that point, you had Margaret Sanger starting up her first clinics in New York.
sentences.zh: 警察把她关进了监狱，就像她在随后的运动中又七次被捕一样。

sentences.en: When Mrs. Margaret Sanger opened the first birth control clinic in the United States back in 1916, birth control was a dirty word.
sentences.zh: 那场运动让桑格夫人长期远离她的孩子。

sentences.en: The police threw her into jail as they were to do seven more times during her crusade.
sentences.zh: 它导致了她第一次婚姻的破裂，她遭受了持续的、令人痛苦的社会虐待。

sentences.en: That crusade kept Mrs. Sanger away from her children for long periods.
sentences.zh: 提醒我一下，玛格丽特·桑格是谁？

sentences.en: It helped to break up her first marriage, and she suffered constant, harrowing social abuse.
sentences.zh: 玛格丽特·桑格是著名的避孕运动先驱。

sentences.en: And just remind me, who is Margaret Sanger?
sentences.zh: 桑格夫人，您不仅在美国，而且在欧洲和东方也帮助传播了避孕运动。

sentences.en: Margaret Sanger was the famous apostle of birth control.
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Mrs. Sanger, you have helped to spread the birth control movement, not only here in the United States, but in Europe and the Orient as well.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是为了拯救女性免受痛苦吗？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 在您看来，这是唯一的原因吗？

sentences.en: Why is it just to save women's suffering?
sentences.zh: 我来自一个大家庭。

sentences.en: Is that the only reason in your mind?
sentences.zh: 我母亲英年早逝。

sentences.en: I came with a large family.
sentences.zh: 十一个孩子。

sentences.en: My mother died young.
sentences.zh: 这给我童年留下了深刻的印象。

sentences.en: Eleven children.
sentences.zh: 她与贫穷的、主要是移民妇女一起工作，她非常清楚这些妇女在拥有庞大、巨大的家庭和许多孩子时所面临的问题，

sentences.en: Made an impression on me as a child.
sentences.zh: 当她们如此贫穷并在国内挣扎时。

sentences.en: She worked with poor, mostly immigrant women, and it was very clear to her the problems that these women were having when they had large, enormous families with many children
sentences.zh: 我看到妇女们请求有一种方法，使她们不必过早地再次怀孕。

sentences.en: when they were so poor and struggling in the country.
sentences.zh: 帮助女性找出如何避免意外怀孕的方法成了她的热情所在。

sentences.en: I saw women who asked to have some means whereby they wouldn't have to have another pregnancy too early.
sentences.zh: 她不仅通过科学地试图找出最有用、最可行和最有效的方法来做到这一点，而且在自己的生活中也提供咨询。

sentences.en: And it became her passion to help women figure out how to avoid unwanted pregnancies.
sentences.zh: 所以，避孕措施在邮寄上仍然是非法的这种情况，正如你所解释的，这是一种非常重要的使用方式。

sentences.en: And she did that both scientifically by trying to figure out what the most useful and viable and effective methods were, but also in her own life in providing counseling.
sentences.zh: 这种情况持续了多久？

sentences.en: So this situation where contraceptions remain illegal to male, which, as you've explained, is a really vital way that they would get used.
sentences.zh: 直到什么时候？

sentences.en: How long does that remain the case?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: Until when?
sentences.zh: 在30年代，突然出现了大萧条，美国人有一种真正的感觉，即拥有太多的孩子是一件危险和麻烦的事情，

sentences.en: What happened?
sentences.zh: 而穷人拥有太多的孩子则是一件更加危险和麻烦的事情。

sentences.en: In the 30s, suddenly you had the Depression, and you had a real sense on the part of Americans that having a whole lot of children was a dangerous and problematic thing,
sentences.zh: 这在当时是社会纯洁运动的基本思维模式。

sentences.en: and that poor people having a lot of children was an even more dangerous and problematic thing.
sentences.zh: 我猜野兽就是那些使用避孕措施的人。

sentences.en: And at that point, when people became so concerned about the number of children, about limiting pregnancies, the federal courts struck down all the federal restrictions.
sentences.zh: 当时，人们对儿童数量和限制怀孕的问题非常关注，联邦法院废除了所有联邦层面的限制。

sentences.en: So in 1938, birth control becomes legal.
sentences.zh: 所以，1938年，避孕变得合法了。

sentences.en: Yeah, federally.
sentences.zh: 是的，在联邦层面。

sentences.en: What happens, though, is that it's happened so often in this country.
sentences.zh: 然而，在这个国家，这种情况经常发生。

sentences.en: Various states went off in different directions.
sentences.zh: 各个州朝着不同的方向发展。

sentences.en: As we're getting into the 50s and the 60s, you have some states where it's very easy to obtain birth control.
sentences.zh: 进入50年代和60年代，有些州获取避孕措施非常容易。

sentences.en: You have some states where it's illegal, completely and totally illegal, to distribute birth control, to tell people, even to give people information
sentences.zh: 而在另一些州，分发避孕用品、告诉人们甚至向人们提供相关信息都是非法的，完全彻底的非法，

sentences.en: about how to control their number of children.
sentences.zh: 关于如何控制子女数量的信息。

sentences.en: Combined preparations containing an estrogen and a progestogen are taken in constant proportions, usually for 21 days, followed by an interval without medication,
sentences.zh: 含有雌激素和孕激素的复合制剂通常按固定比例服用，通常服用21天，随后是停药期，

sentences.en: during which uterine bleeding occurs.
sentences.zh: 在此期间会出现子宫出血。

sentences.en: So how do we get from there to the pill?
sentences.zh: 那么我们是如何从那时走到避孕药的呢？

sentences.en: The pill comes along in the 1960s and a lot of women just can't get their hands on it.
sentences.zh: 避孕药在20世纪60年代出现，但很多女性根本无法获得。

sentences.en: It just depends on where you are.
sentences.zh: 这完全取决于你身处何地。

sentences.en: And the problem was with poor women who needed to go to clinics and the clinics were not allowed to help them in any way.
sentences.zh: 问题在于那些需要去诊所的贫困女性，而诊所被禁止以任何方式帮助她们。

sentences.en: They were not allowed to give them information in many states.
sentences.zh: 在许多州，诊所被禁止向她们提供信息。

sentences.en: They were not allowed to prescribe birth control pills.
sentences.zh: 她们被禁止开避孕药处方。

sentences.en: And what's the significance of the pill culturally when it's developed in the 1960s?
sentences.zh: 那么，避孕药在20世纪60年代被开发出来，在文化上有什么意义呢？

sentences.en: Before the pill, really, if you wanted to be a career woman, a career professional, you were probably not going to want to get married.
sentences.zh: 在避孕药出现之前，如果你想成为一名职业女性、一名专业人士，你可能就不想结婚了。

sentences.en: And the idea for young women of having to choose between marriage and a career, generally that tended in the end to be the career that lost out.
sentences.zh: 对于年轻女性来说，必须在婚姻和事业之间做出选择，通常最终往往是事业做出了牺牲。

sentences.en: But suddenly, that's all done.
sentences.zh: 但突然之间，这一切都结束了。

sentences.en: And a woman can get married, she can have children when she has the right time to have children, or she cannot have children, and she can have a career.
sentences.zh: 女性可以结婚，可以在合适的时机生孩子，也可以选择不生孩子，同时还能拥有自己的事业。

sentences.en: And it transformed immediately the number of women that you saw going to medical school, to law school, to becoming professionals of every kind.
sentences.zh: 它立即改变了进入医学院、法学院以及成为各类专业人士的女性人数。

sentences.en: It was absolutely transformative.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是变革性的。

sentences.en: So many states outlawed the pill, but of course, we know that's no longer the case that is outlawed.
sentences.zh: 很多州曾取缔避孕药，但当然，我们知道现在情况已经不再是这样了。

sentences.en: So what exactly happened?
sentences.zh: 那么到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, you had several critical cases in which the Supreme Court basically said, guys, you can't do this anymore.
sentences.zh: 好吧，有几个关键案件，最高法院基本上说，伙计们，你们不能再这样做了。

sentences.en: Number 496, Estelle T.
sentences.zh: 第496号，埃斯特尔·T·

sentences.en: Griswold et al.
sentences.zh: 格里斯沃尔德等人。

sentences.en: Fellance v.
sentences.zh: 诉

sentences.en: Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 康涅狄格州。

sentences.en: The first big one in 1965 was Griswold v.
sentences.zh: 1965年的第一个重大案件是格里斯沃尔德诉

sentences.en: Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 康涅狄格州案。

sentences.en: In Connecticut, it was illegal to transmit any information about birth control, let alone give out birth control, give out even condoMs.
sentences.zh: 在康涅狄格州，传播任何关于避孕的信息都是非法的，更不用说分发避孕用品，甚至分发避孕套了。

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, may it please the court?
sentences.zh: 首席大法官先生，请允许我发言？

sentences.en: This case involves the validity of the Connecticut anti-contraceptive statute.
sentences.zh: 本案涉及康涅狄格州反避孕法规的有效性。

sentences.en: So the Planned Parenthood wanted to do something about that, and they set up a case in which they arranged to get people arrested.
sentences.zh: 所以计划生育协会想对此采取行动，他们策划了一起案件，安排人员被捕。

sentences.en: The procedure was that when a married woman came to the center, she was interviewed, and various forms of contraception were explained to her.
sentences.zh: 程序是这样的：当已婚妇女来到中心时，她会接受访谈，并向她解释各种避孕方式。

sentences.en: So there were women who volunteered to be part of it, and doctors who had volunteered gave them information, prescribed birth control pills, gave them the birth control pills,
sentences.zh: 所以有一些女性自愿参与其中，自愿参与的医生向她们提供了信息，开了避孕药处方，并给了她们避孕药，

sentences.en: and then they were arrested.
sentences.zh: 然后她们就被捕了。

sentences.en: And in fact, this was so set up that they were able, rather than to be dramatically arrested in the clinic, they just went to the police station.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是精心策划的，他们没有在诊所里戏剧性地被捕，而是直接去了警察局。

sentences.en: They volunteered themselves to the police as people who have violated the law.
sentences.zh: 他们向警方自首，承认自己违反了法律。

sentences.en: Right, and that gave them a standing to take the case to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 没错，这给了他们将案件诉至最高法院的资格。

sentences.en: So Planned Parenthood is knowingly abating states like Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 所以计划生育协会是在明知故犯地挑战像康涅狄格州这样的州。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then what happens?
sentences.zh: 然后发生了什么？

sentences.en: The Supreme Court ruled that married people had a right to get information on birth control from clinics or anywhere else.
sentences.zh: 最高法院裁定，已婚人士有权从诊所或其他任何地方获取避孕信息。

sentences.en: Wait, married people, you're saying?
sentences.zh: 等等，你是说已婚人士？

sentences.en: Married people, yeah.
sentences.zh: 已婚人士，是的。

sentences.en: So what about unmarried women?
sentences.zh: 那未婚女性呢？

sentences.en: Could they not get birth control legally?
sentences.zh: 她们不能合法获得避孕措施吗？

sentences.en: Unmarried women, in theory, were still a problem.
sentences.zh: 理论上，未婚女性仍然是个问题。

sentences.en: But the birth control crusader
sentences.zh: 但避孕倡导者

sentences.en: Bill Baird took up the cause in Massachusetts and arranged a few years later to get arrested giving condoms, I think it was, to an unmarried woman.
sentences.zh: 比尔·贝尔德在马萨诸塞州接过了这项事业，几年后安排自己因向一名未婚女性分发避孕套（我想是这样）而被捕。

sentences.en: And then he went to court and in a case,
sentences.zh: 然后他上了法庭，在一场案件中，

sentences.en: Baird v.
sentences.zh: 贝尔德诉

sentences.en: Eisenstadt, he won.
sentences.zh: 艾森斯塔特案，他赢了。

sentences.en: And that was the end of the laws against birth control pills.
sentences.zh: 这就是针对避孕药的法律的终结。

sentences.en: The Baird case was decided in 1972.
sentences.zh: 贝尔德案于1972年裁决。

sentences.en: And that's about the time, by the way, that the states are required under Medicaid to provide birth control services.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，大约在那个时候，各州被要求根据医疗补助计划提供避孕服务。

sentences.en: So you're simultaneously having a great leap right there into our present life.
sentences.zh: 所以你同时看到了我们现在生活中的一大飞跃。

sentences.en: And what's the significance of Medicaid suddenly requiring in some way that birth control be covered?
sentences.zh: 那么，医疗补助计划突然以某种方式要求覆盖避孕服务，这有什么意义呢？

sentences.en: You know, the problem of getting access to contraceptives is not a financial one if you're middle class.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你是中产阶级，获取避孕药具的问题不是经济问题。

sentences.en: But if you're working class struggling,
sentences.zh: 但如果你是苦苦挣扎的工薪阶层，

sentences.en: I mean, this stuff can become very expensive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些东西可能会变得非常昂贵。

sentences.en: And this was the moment at which people who were poor enough to receive Medicaid also were able to get as part of that package contraceptives.
sentences.zh: 而就在那一刻，贫困到可以享受医疗补助的人们也能够将避孕药具作为该计划的一部分获得。

sentences.en: The only person who should get to make decisions about your health is you.
sentences.zh: 唯一应该对你的健康做出决定的人就是你自己。

sentences.en: That's why we fought so hard to make health care reform a reality.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们如此努力地使医疗改革成为现实。

sentences.en: So the Affordable Care Act, which we see in 2010, is suddenly requiring employers to provide contraception at basically no cost, which sounds like a big breakthrough.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在2010年看到的《平价医疗法案》，突然要求雇主基本上免费提供避孕措施，这听起来像是一个重大突破。

sentences.en: Because of the ACA, most insurance plans are now covering the cost of contraceptive care so that a working mom doesn't have to put off the care she needs just so she can
sentences.zh: 由于《平价医疗法案》，大多数保险计划现在都覆盖了避孕护理的费用，这样一位工作的母亲就不必为了

sentences.en: pay her bills on time.
sentences.zh: 按时支付账单而推迟她需要的护理。

sentences.en: But that breakthrough has immediate kind of cultural consequences.
sentences.zh: 但这种突破有直接的文化后果。

sentences.en: Well, it has cultural consequences and it has legal consequences in that
sentences.zh: 嗯，它有文化后果，也有法律后果，因为

sentences.en: religious groups argued that they should not have to pay for something that they believed was immoral.
sentences.zh: 宗教团体辩称，他们不应该为他们认为不道德的事情买单。

sentences.en: and the administration, the Obama administration, in the end, worked out a plan whereby
sentences.zh: 而政府，奥巴马政府，最终制定了一项计划，

sentences.en: religious organizations who did not want to provide coverage for their employees could refuse to do so.
sentences.zh: 不想为员工提供避孕覆盖的宗教组织可以拒绝这样做。

sentences.en: The insurers would provide the coverage anyway and the government would pay the difference.
sentences.zh: 保险公司无论如何都会提供覆盖，政府会支付差额。

sentences.en: So it seems like everybody was happy.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来每个人都很高兴。

sentences.en: Nobody is ever always happy in this country.
sentences.zh: 在这个国家，没有人能永远高兴。

sentences.en: My administration is leading by example as we take historic steps to protect religious liberty in the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 我的政府正在以身作则，我们正在采取历史性步骤来保护美利坚合众国的宗教自由。

sentences.en: We will not allow people of faith to be targeted, bullied, or silenced anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们不会再允许有信仰的人被针对、欺凌或噤声。

sentences.en: So what is this all about, what President Trump has done?
sentences.zh: 那么这一切到底是怎么回事，特朗普总统做了什么？

sentences.en: It's something that he promised during the campaign and now he's delivering.
sentences.zh: 这是他在竞选期间承诺的事情，现在他正在兑现。

sentences.en: And he has a lot of supporters who don't like the idea of government messing with businesses, government making rules about what businesses can do and they don't like government
sentences.zh: 他有很多支持者，他们不喜欢政府干涉企业，不喜欢政府制定关于企业能做什么的规则，他们不喜欢政府

sentences.en: messing in with anything.
sentences.zh: 干涉任何事情。

sentences.en: And so anything that says government's not going to do this anymore tends to be welcome.
sentences.zh: 所以任何说政府不再这样做的事情往往都会受到欢迎。

sentences.en: And you do have a very strong segment of his support group that really, really cares about these kinds of issues, issues having to do with sexual behavior and they'll
sentences.zh: 而且你确实拥有他支持群体中非常强大的一部分，他们真的非常关心这类问题，即与性行为有关的问题，他们也会

sentences.en: be pleased too.
sentences.zh: 感到高兴。

sentences.en: And the people who are upset or worried or concerned are not in general his base.
sentences.zh: 而那些感到不安、担忧或关切的人，通常不是他的基本盘。

sentences.en: So finally,
sentences.zh: 所以最后，

sentences.en: Gail, what happens now?
sentences.zh: 盖尔，现在会发生什么？

sentences.en: Do we know the actual impact or do we suspect that we know the actual impact of what this change is going to be?
sentences.zh: 我们知道实际影响吗，还是我们怀疑我们知道这种变化将带来的实际影响？

sentences.en: Potentially, there's a vast number of women who could lose their contraceptive coverage in their health care plans.
sentences.zh: 潜在地，有大量的女性可能会在她们的医疗保险计划中失去避孕覆盖。

sentences.en: We don't in reality know how many there are going to be and we don't know what kind of precedent this is going to set for other stuff that this administration wants to do.
sentences.zh: 实际上我们不知道会有多少人，也不知道这将为本届政府想要做的其他事情开创什么样的先例。

sentences.en: And we don't know how many women this will affect because we don't know how many businesses would choose to claim a moral objection, which is now allowed by
sentences.zh: 我们不知道这会影响多少女性，因为我们不知道有多少企业会选择提出道德反对，这现在是被

sentences.en: President Trump to providing birth control.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统允许的，从而拒绝提供避孕措施。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Thank you,
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，

sentences.en: Gail.
sentences.zh: 盖尔。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: No problem.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: Good to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他事情。

sentences.en: This is my neighborhood
sentences.zh: 这是我的社区，

sentences.en: in flames,
sentences.zh: 陷入火海，

sentences.en: completely in flames.
sentences.zh: 完全陷入火海。

sentences.en: Wildfires are raging across
sentences.zh: 野火正在肆虐

sentences.en: Northern California, killing at least
sentences.zh: 北加州，造成至少

sentences.en: 10 people and forcing the evacuation of as many as 20,000 in one of the most destructive fire emergencies in the state's history.
sentences.zh: 10人死亡，并迫使多达2万人撤离，这是该州历史上最具破坏性的火灾紧急情况之一。
